_note: Executable spec for RecommendationEngine. Amounts CAD unless stated. Expected values are exact engine outputs (unrounded beyond 4dp); UI rounds to cents at display. Valuations: MR pinned to 1.8¢ by pinnedValuations below (owner-state.json now ranks at the 1.0¢ floor), MBNA 1.0¢, Bonvoy 0.8¢, cash 1:1, CT ×0.95, CRO ×1.0 auto-sold / ×0.8 held. Default card wealthsimple-vip; threshold both(0.5pp, $0.25). Base owner state per owner-state.json: rogersEligibleServiceLinked=false, cryptoLevelUpProActive=false, Tangerine treatAsAllSelected (2% hypothetical everywhere — can only tie WS, never clears threshold), Scotia 4% cap progress $12,500. Ties rank the default card first. Every case is evaluated at asOf 2026-08-20 unless it declares its own "asOf" — effective-dating is the one rule family that cannot be exercised at a single fixed date.

pinnedValuations._why: These 27 cases document ENGINE BEHAVIOUR and are pinned to an above-floor MR value so they exercise points-vs-cash ranking. They deliberately do NOT track owner-state.json, whose live setting is the 1.0¢ cash floor — otherwise every valuation change would re-baseline the whole spec and the temptation would be to accept engine output rather than re-derive the arithmetic.

cases.description: The same $80 utility bill, but the terminal submits MCC 4816 — outside mbna-utilities-5x's include list, so the rule is excluded

Winner = WS is therefore proof the exclusion fired. Field: Cobalt/Platinum base 1x = 200 x 1.8c = $3.60; Bonvoy 400 x 0.8c = $3.20; Rogers 1.5% = $3.00; MBNA and Scotia $2.00; Triangle CT$2.00 x 0.95 = $1.90; Tangerine 0.5% = $1.00 ('other' is not a selected category). Note the contrast with mccInclude: mccExclude is also skipped when purchase.mcc is nil, but skipping it is PERMISSIVE for the cardholder there and here - the two gates fail in the same direction on unknown data, which is only safe for one of them.

cases.description: Recurring insurance premium $120 evaluated on 2026-02-01 — the exact effectiveFrom day of every Scotia Momentum rule

expected.notes: RuleMatcher.isLive compares ISO date strings lexicographically: '2026-02-01' <= '2026-02-01' is true, so effectiveFrom is INCLUSIVE. Scotia's 4% fires through the 'recurring' pseudo-category, which matches() evaluates before and independently of mccInclude (the include list is consulted only inside the default category branch), so MCC 6300 is irrelevant and the rate is 4% x $120 = $4.80 - cap momentum-4pct-accountYear sits at $12,500 of $25,000, room $12,500 >> $120 so no split, and $12,500 < 90% x $25,000 so no capNearlyExhausted. WS and Tangerine each earn 2% = $2.40; advantage $2.40 = 2.00pp, both floors clear. Tangerine matches because recurring is selected and the purchase recurringIndicator is true. Field: Cobalt/Platinum 120 x 1.8c = $2.16; Bonvoy 240 x 0.8c = $1.92; Rogers 1.5% = $1.80; MBNA 1x = $1.20; Triangle CT$1.20 x 0.95 = $1.14. Paired with scotia-effective-from-day-before-120.

cases.description: The same premium one day earlier, 2026-01-31 — every Scotia rule is pre-effective, so the card has no scorable rule at all

expected.notes: One day earlier and the flip is total. '2026-02-01' <= '2026-01-31' is false lexicographically, so ALL THREE Scotia rules - momentum-base included - fail isLive, RuleMatcher finds no candidate, and Scorer excludes the card. Scotia's $4.80 vanishes and the default takes it back: WS and Tangerine each earn 2% x 120 = $2.40 because recurring is selected on Tangerine; the default wins the tie and Tangerine is runner-up. The day-of/day-before pair is the assertion; it pins both the inclusive boundary and the fact that a card whose ENTIRE rule set is pre-effective drops out rather than falling back to some implicit base rate. valuationSensitive false: at 2.2c Cobalt reaches $2.64, but the flip needs $2.40 + max($0.25, 0.5pp x $120 = $0.60) = $3.00 -> 2.50c/pt, past the 2.2c benchmark.

cases.description: US$ purchase of C$2,000 evaluated 2026-08-20 — Crypto's announced 2026-09-01 FX record must not apply yet

expected.notes: activeFxRule takes the FIRST record whose window contains asOf. Record 1 (status current, effectiveTo 2026-08-31, rate 0) contains 2026-08-20, so the announced record - effectiveFrom 2026-09-01, freeAllowanceCadPerCalendarMonth C$1,400, postAllowanceRate 2% - is never consulted. Earn: 3% x $2,000 = 60 CRO x 1.0 (auto-sold) = $60.00, minus 0% FX = $60.00. The cap is measured in USD: no usdEquivalent supplied, so Scorer's fallback gives 2000 x 0.73 = US$1,460 < US$2,500, fully in-cap. WS 2% = $40.00 (0% FX). Advantage $20.00 = 1.00pp. THE ASSERTION IS THE ABSENT WARNING: both FX records carry rate 0, so the two windows are dollar-identical and only fxAllowanceAssumed distinguishes them - without warningsAbsent this case would pass even if the announced record were applied a fortnight early. Field, all net of 2.5% FX = $50.00: Rogers USD 3% = $60.00 - $50.00 = $10.00; Cobalt/Platinum $36.00 - $50.00 = -$14.00; Bonvoy -$18.00; MBNA and Scotia -$30.00; Triangle -$31.00; Tangerine -$40.00. Paired with crypto-fx-allowance-assumed-2026-09-01.

cases.description: The same US$ purchase one day later — the announced record takes over and the engine declares the free-allowance assumption instead of pricing it

expected.notes: Record 1 expires ('2026-09-01' <= '2026-08-31' is false) and the announced record becomes active. Scorer's FX branch is all-or-nothing: freeAllowanceCadPerCalendarMonth present -> charge NOTHING and raise fxAllowanceAssumed. Net stays $60.00, byte-identical to the day before, and only the warning moves. DECLARED-NOT-COMPUTED, and the amount is chosen to show the size of the gap: the allowance is C$1,400 per calendar month, so this single C$2,000 purchase already overruns it by C$600, and postAllowanceRate 2% would cost $12.00 - the defensible number is $48.00, not $60.00, and the advantage over WS would be $8.00 rather than $20.00. The engine does not track month-to-date foreign spend, so it declares the assumption rather than pricing it; both fields are marked x-status declared-not-computed in card-catalogue.schema.json. The winner does not change here, but it would wherever the margin is under the unpriced FX.

cases.description: $400 at a Mastercard-only merchant with rogers-enhanced-accountYear fully consumed and an eligible service linked — appliedRuleId names the 2% rule while every dollar earns the 1.5% postCapEarn

It is the complement of cobalt-cap-exhausted-100, which asserts that exhaustion makes the winner FLIP; here the exhausted card still wins, at its post-cap rate, so the post-cap arithmetic is itself the asserted number. Pairing winnerRule 'rogers-base-2-with-service' with a 1.5% outcome is deliberate: appliedRuleId names the rule that MATCHED, never the rate actually paid, and any UI that renders '2%' from appliedRuleId would overstate this checkout by $2.00. Field - Mastercard only, so WS and Scotia (Visa) and all three Amex cards are gated out, hence defaultNotAccepted: MBNA base 1x = 400 x 1.0c = $4.00; Triangle base 1% = CT$4.00 x 0.95 = $3.80; Tangerine base 0.5% = $2.00 ('other' unselected). capNearlyExhausted: $61,000 >= 90% x $61,000. WestJet base 1.5x = 400 x 1.5 = 600 pts x 1.0c = $6.00; MBNA's $4.00 drops to third. 2026-08-20: westjet-rbc-world-elite became scorable when programs.json valued westJetPoints, and it TIES the winner exactly — 1.5 WestJet points per dollar at the posted 1.0¢ is 1.5%, the same rate Rogers pays in cash. rank() breaks the tie on cardId ascending, so 'rogers-red-we' < 'westjet-rbc-world-elite' keeps the winner unchanged and takes second place off MBNA. The tie itself is pinned separately by westjet-rogers-exact-tie-100.

cases.description: $1,000 specialty-grocer order (MCC 5451) with Cobalt's eats cap at $2,420 — Cobalt beats the default by $3.76 but only 0.376pp, so 'both' semantics holds the default

expected.notes: The MIRROR of taxi-12-threshold-suppression: there the pp floor was met and the CAD floor missed; here the CAD floor is met and the pp floor missed. The two together pin 'both' from both sides - under 'either' semantics BOTH would switch, which is exactly the reading owner-state.json flagged for veto. Cobalt: room = $2,500 - $2,420 = $80, so $80 x 5 + $920 x 1 = 1,320 MR x 1.8c = $23.76, with capNearlyExhausted ($2,420 >= $2,250). WS 2% = $20.00. Advantage $3.76: 0.376pp < the 0.5pp floor (fails), $3.76 >= the $0.25 floor (passes) -> held. MCC 5451 is doing quiet work here: it keeps mbna-grocery-5x (needs 5411/5462/5499), triangle-grocery-3pct (5411) and momentum-grocery-recurring-4pct (5411) all at base, leaving Cobalt - whose cobalt-eats-5x carries no mccInclude at all - as the only accelerated card. Field: Tangerine 2% = $20.00 (ties the default; ties rank the default first); Platinum 1,000 x 1.8c = $18.00; Bonvoy 2,000 x 0.8c = $16.00; Rogers 1.5% = $15.00; MBNA and Scotia $10.00; Triangle CT$10.00 x 0.95 = $9.50. TWO BEHAVIOURS WORTH NAMING. (a) runnerUp is $23.76 while the winner is $20.00 - when the threshold holds the default, runnerUp is 'the card you passed up', not 'second best', and any UI sorting on runnerUpValueCad must expect it to exceed the winner. (b) The upside breakeven is 1.8939c = ($20.00 + max($0.25, 0.5pp x $1,000 = $5.00)) x 100 / 1,320 pts, which is BELOW the declared 1.8c and inside the 2.2c benchmark, so it is disclosed: at this margin the breakeven is the point where Cobalt clears the SWITCH THRESHOLD, not the point where it overtakes on raw value - it already has.

cases.description: The same $1,000 order with the cap $20 lower ($2,400) — advantage lands at 0.520pp and the switch is recommended

expected.notes: Twenty dollars less cap usage than threshold-both-cad-cleared-pp-missed-1000, and the verdict inverts. Room $100 -> $100 x 5 + $900 x 1 = 1,400 MR x 1.8c = $25.20. Advantage over WS's $20.00 is $5.20 = 0.520pp: >= 0.5pp and >= $0.25, so both floors clear and the switch is recommended. The pp floor is the binding constraint and the exact break is $5.00 of advantage - 1,388.9 pts, i.e. cap room $97.22 - so these two cases bracket a real edge rather than a comfortable one. Field is unchanged from the paired case. The disclosed direction flips to 'below' because the winner is now a points card that only wins at the declared 1.8c: at the 1.0c MR floor Cobalt is 1,400 x 1.0c = $14.00 and the default takes it back, so the engine discloses the DOWNSIDE breakeven 1.7857c = ($20.00 + $5.00) x 100 / 1,400 pts. Read together the pair also pins ordering: RecommendationEngine checks downside before upside, so one purchase can disclose at most one direction.

cases.description: $400 recurring specialty-grocer charge — Scotia's 4% wins in dollars, Cobalt would win at 2.00¢/MR, and 2.00¢ is inside the 2.2¢ published benchmark, so the upside is disclosed

expected.notes: Scotia via the recurring branch: 4% x $400 = $16.00 (cap at $12,500 of $25,000 - no split, no warning). Cobalt: room $100 -> $100 x 5 + $300 x 1 = 800 MR x 1.8c = $14.40, capNearlyExhausted. WS 2% = $8.00; advantage $8.00 = 2.00pp, so the switch is recommended. THE UPSIDE GATE IN FULL: at the 2.2c benchmark Cobalt is 800 x 2.2c = $17.60 > Scotia's $16.00, so the challenger genuinely overtakes and clears the threshold at benchmark. Breakeven = needed x 100 / units, where needed = max(incumbent Scotia $16.00, default WS $8.00 + max($0.25, 0.5pp x $400 = $2.00) = $10.00) = $16.00, giving $16.00 x 100 / 800 = 2.00c/pt. 2.00c <= 2.20c benchmark -> DISCLOSED. Field: Tangerine 2% = $8.00 (ties WS; default first); Platinum 400 x 1.8c = $7.20; Bonvoy 800 x 0.8c = $6.40; Rogers 1.5% = $6.00; MBNA base 1x = $4.00 (5451 not in its grocery list); Triangle base CT$4.00 x 0.95 = $3.80. Paired with valuation-upside-withheld-outside-benchmark-400.

cases.description: The same $400 grocer charge, NOT recurring and with the Cobalt cap at $2,490 — the flip needs 2.2727¢/MR, past the 2.2¢ benchmark, so nothing is disclosed

expected.notes: Not recurring, so Scotia drops to base 1% = $4.00 and the incumbent is the default itself. Cobalt: room $10 -> $10 x 5 + $390 x 1 = 440 MR x 1.8c = $7.92, just under WS's $8.00, with capNearlyExhausted. THE GATE: at 2.2c Cobalt reaches 440 x 2.2c = $9.68 and beats $8.00 on raw value - but the flip must also clear the switch threshold, so needed = $8.00 + max($0.25, 0.5pp x $400 = $2.00) = $10.00, giving $10.00 x 100 / 440 = 2.2727c/pt > the 2.20c benchmark -> WITHHELD, valuationSensitive false. This is the boundary the disclosure rule exists to draw: 2.00c inside (previous case) versus 2.2727c outside, a 27-hundredths-of-a-cent difference in what the owner is told. In practice the gate bites twice, because the aspirational ranking is a full Verdict and the threshold has already suppressed Cobalt there ($9.68 - $8.00 = $1.68 = 0.42pp < 0.5pp) before the explicit flip <= benchmarkCents check runs. runnerUp is Tangerine, tied with the default at 2%: ties rank the default first, and runnerUp when the default holds is the best NON-default card. Field: Platinum $7.20; Bonvoy $6.40; Rogers $6.00; MBNA and Scotia $4.00; Triangle $3.80.

cases.description: $300 at a Mastercard-only merchant with rogersEligibleServiceLinked forced back to unresolved (nil) — the 2% rule is skipped rather than guessed

expected.notes: conditionsResolveTrue tests `state.rogersEligibleServiceLinked == true`, so nil and false take the same branch: the rule is dropped, never guessed in either direction. rogers-base-2-with-service is skipped and the unconditional rogers-base-1_5 carries the card at 1.5% x $300 = $4.50 (cap room $61,000, no split). Had the condition resolved true the same purchase would earn 2% = $6.00, so asserting BOTH winnerRule and $4.50 is what pins fail-closed. owner-state.json resolves this field to false rather than nil, so the fixture uses unsetFields to reach the genuinely-unresolved state; the outcome is identical, and that identity is itself the contract a TS twin must reproduce - unresolved is not a third state at the engine boundary, it collapses into 'condition not met'. Compare utilities-nil-mcc-permissive-fallback-80, where unknown DATA (a nil MCC) resolves permissively while unknown OWNER STATE resolves restrictively. Field: MBNA base 1x = 300 x 1.0c = $3.00; Triangle base 1% = CT$3.00 x 0.95 = $2.85; Tangerine base 0.5% = $1.50 ('other' unselected). WS and Scotia are Visa and the Amex cards are gated, hence defaultNotAccepted. WestJet base 1.5x = 300 x 1.5 = 450 pts x 1.0c = $4.50, an exact tie with the winner, so it takes second place off MBNA's $3.00 on cardId ascending; see westjet-rogers-exact-tie-100.

cases.description: $100 at a Mastercard-only merchant where WestJet's 1.5 points/$ at 1.0¢ and Rogers' 1.5% cash are worth exactly the same — the tie is broken by cardId, not by value

expected.notes: Exists because three other cases (costco-mastercard-only-200, rogers-cap-exhausted-postcap-400, owner-condition-unresolved-rogers-300) started depending on a tie-break nobody had asserted. WestJet earns 1.5 points per dollar and westJetPoints is valued at the posted 1.0c, so 100 x 1.5 = 150 pts x 1.0c = $1.50 - identical, to the cent, to Rogers paying 1.5 percent cash on $100. rank() sorts on value descending and falls through to cardId ASCENDING, so 'rogers-red-we' < 'westjet-rbc-world-elite' decides it. That is deterministic but arbitrary: the engine is not claiming Rogers is better, it is claiming the two are indistinguishable and something had to go first. Pinning it here means a future re-order, a renamed cardId, or a WestJet revaluation fails ONE case that says why, instead of three that look like unrelated regressions. valuationSensitive is false and that is the second fact worth having: westJetPoints has no cash-out, so it sets no floorCentsPerPoint and Scorer falls back to centsPerPoint - the floor band collapses onto the declared band, and the engine cannot warn that this tie rests entirely on WestJet points being worth face value to an owner who flies WestJet. Field - Mastercard only, so WS and Scotia (Visa) and the Amex cards are gated, hence defaultNotAccepted: MBNA base 1x = 100 x 1.0c = $1.00; NBC base 1x = 100 x 1.0c = $1.00; Amazon base 1x = 100 x 1.0c = $1.00; Triangle base 1 percent = CT$1.00 x 0.95 = $0.95; BMO Ascend base 1x = 100 x 0.666667c = $0.67; PC Insiders base 10ppd = 1,000 pts x 0.1c = $1.00; Tangerine base 0.5 percent = $0.50 ('other' unselected).

cases.description: $300 at a Mastercard-only merchant with rogersEligibleServiceLinked answered TRUE through CardState.flags while the legacy named property still reads false — flags wins and the 2% rule fires

expected.notes: THE PRECEDENCE RULE, and until now it lived only in a doc comment. owner-state.json resolves rogers-red-we's legacy `rogersEligibleServiceLinked` to FALSE; this override sets only `flags`, leaving that stale mirror untouched, so `resolvedFlags` must fold the legacy value in FIRST and let `flags` overwrite it. Get the merge order backwards and the legacy false wins, rogers-base-2-with-service is skipped, and the case lands on $4.50 instead - which is exactly the outcome of owner-condition-unresolved-rogers-300, its deliberate minimal pair. That $1.50 gap is the whole assertion: a state written by a NEW build and read alongside an OLD mirror must not be clobbered by the mirror, and that is the property any migration off the legacy properties depends on. Earn = 2% x $300 = $6.00; cap room is the full $61,000 from zero, so no split and no capNearlyExhausted. Field - Mastercard only, so WS and Scotia (Visa) and all three Amex cards are gated out, hence defaultNotAccepted: WestJet base 1.5x = 300 x 1.5 = 450 pts x 1.0c = $4.50; MBNA base 1x = $3.00; Triangle base 1% = CT$3.00 x 0.95 = $2.85; Tangerine base 0.5% = $1.50 ('other' unselected).

cases.description: The same $300 purchase with rogersEligibleServiceLinked answered FALSE in flags — an explicit no is indistinguishable from unanswered at the engine boundary

expected.notes: Byte-identical expectations to owner-condition-unresolved-rogers-300, reached from a DIFFERENT input, and the identity is the point. `flags` stores three states - true, false, absent - because a UI must know which cards still owe an answer, but the engine collapses false and absent into one: `flags[condition] ?? false`. An implementation that tested key PRESENCE (`flags[condition] != nil`) rather than its value would pass every other fixture in this file and fail only here, paying the owner 2% for having answered 'no'. Paired with flags-beat-stale-legacy-mirror-300, the same purchase with the one boolean flipped, $1.50 apart.

cases.description: $100 at Amazon.ca with amazonEligiblePrimeLinked answered true — the 2.5x rule beats the whole wallet

expected.notes: Prime linked: amazon-ca-prime-2_5x earns 100 x 2.5 = 250 Amazon Rewards points; programs.json posts 1.0c/pt, so 250 x $0.01 = $2.50. The unconditional amazon-ca-nonprime-1_5x also matches the merchant, but RuleMatcher chooses the higher raw earn, so 2.5x wins the card. Whole-wallet field: default Wealthsimple 2% = $2.00; Cobalt and Platinum base 1x = 100 x 1.8c = $1.80; Bonvoy base 2x = 200 x 0.8c = $1.60; Rogers base 1.5% and WestJet base 1.5x at 1.0c are $1.50; MBNA and Scotia base are $1.00; Triangle CT$1.00 x 0.95 = $0.95; Tangerine base 0.5% = $0.50 ('other' is unselected); Crypto is excluded because Level Up Pro is inactive. Advantage over the default is $2.50 - $2.00 = $0.50, or 0.50pp; both switch floors ($0.25 and 0.50pp) clear exactly. This winner could not occur before card-contracts@2.10: 2.8 made the flag answerable, while 2.10 removes the independent scoredInV1 gate that still kept the rule unpayable.

cases.description: The same $100 Amazon.ca purchase with no Prime answer — 2.5x fails closed and the realistic all-network wallet stays on Wealthsimple

expected.notes: No amazonEligiblePrimeLinked key means the conditional amazon-ca-prime-2_5x rule fails closed. The Amazon card falls to amazon-ca-nonprime-1_5x: 100 x 1.5 = 150 points x 1.0c = $1.50. That card-level rule is pinned directly in the Swift and Kotlin RuleMatcher tests because an end-to-end fixture can assert only winnerRule, and truthful Amazon.ca acceptance leaves Amazon below the top two. Whole-wallet field: default Wealthsimple 2% = $2.00; Cobalt and Platinum base 1x = $1.80 each, with Cobalt taking runner-up by cardId; Bonvoy base 2x = $1.60; Amazon, Rogers and WestJet are $1.50 each, with Amazon first inside that tie by cardId; MBNA and Scotia are $1.00; Triangle is $0.95; Tangerine is $0.50; Crypto is excluded. If unanswered state incorrectly enabled 2.5x, Amazon would jump from $1.50 to $2.50 and flip the asserted winner, so this whole-wallet golden decisively pins fail-closed behavior without inventing a Mastercard-only Amazon acceptance constraint.

cases.description: CIBC Dividend Visa Infinite base rule uses capIds only; $100 straddles its remaining $50 of global room

expected.notes: The CIBC base rule deliberately has capId: null and capIds: [cibc-dividend-vi-global-50k]. Before the purchase, $49,950 of the $50,000 global cap is used, leaving $50: CapMath splits $50 in-cap and $50 over-cap. Both portions earn 1%, because this base rule's postCapEarn is also 1%, so the value remains $1.00; capNearlyExhausted is the decisive representation assertion. A consumer that ignores capIds scores the same dollar value but omits the warning, so this case fails. Wealthsimple remains the Visa-only wallet winner at 2% = $2.00. The accelerated CIBC rules stay gated by cap.globalGroup and cap.statementYear; this fixture does not activate either capability.

cases.description: CIBC Dividend Visa Infinite base rule uses capIds only; its global cap is fully consumed

expected.notes: The same plural-only rule with usage exactly at its $50,000 limit: all $100 is over-cap and earns the cap's 1% fallback, for $1.00. capNearlyExhausted must still appear on the named CIBC candidate. Ignoring capIds omits that warning and fails the fixture. Wealthsimple remains the Visa-only winner at $2.00. Paired with cibc-plural-cap-partial-straddle-100 so the shared contract covers both a partial split and zero remaining room without enabling the still-unsupported accelerated-rule capabilities.
